notes: Strong disagreement on central mechanistic claim. LLM finds the Bax/Bak role in MPTP-dependent necrosis well-supported by converging evidence. Peer reviewers accept observational data but question the interpretation that Bax/Bak are part of the outer membrane MPTP component, requesting additional experiments to confirm this mechanistic model.
Both agree that DKO MEFs show resistance to multiple death stimuli and that reconstitution experiments validate Bax/Bak involvement. This observational phenotype is accepted by both evaluators.

Both accept the in vivo cardiac protection data as valid observations. The ischemia-reperfusion injury protection and reduced MI lethality are treated as established findings by both LLM and peer reviewers.

Both accept the observational data showing differential swelling between wild-type and DKO mitochondria. The factual observations from swelling assays across multiple tissue sources are not questioned, though interpretation differs elsewhere.
Both accept the electron microscopy data showing differential mitochondrial swelling. The structural evidence and quantitative analysis are treated as valid observations by both evaluators.

LLM finds reconstitution experiments with recombinant Bax, gossypol, and permeabilizing agents strongly support the outer membrane permeabilization model. Peer reviewers request alamethicin controls to confirm these agents restore swelling specifically through outer membrane permeabilization rather than other mechanisms.

Partial overlap (C75, C77). LLM supports the outer membrane permeabilization interpretation. Peer reviewers question whether effects are MPTP-specific or represent general outer membrane properties, requesting experiments with non-MPTP swelling agents.

LLM finds non-oligomerizing Bax mutant data strongly support mechanistic distinction between apoptosis and necrosis. Peer reviewers do not directly challenge the data but express uncertainty about mechanistic interpretation, requesting experiments to distinguish MPTP-specific from general outer membrane effects.

LLM finds patch clamp data strongly support that Bax/Bak function at outer membrane without affecting inner membrane MPTP. Peer reviewers acknowledge MPTP is an inner membrane event but question the relationship between outer membrane properties and inner membrane MPTP function, requesting clarifying experiments.

Both accept the patch clamp data showing reduced outer membrane conductance in DKO mitochondria as valid electrophysiological observations, though peer reviewers question the mechanistic interpretation regarding MPTP elsewhere.

Partial overlap (C54, C55, C56). LLM finds calcium uptake capacity measurements provide quantitative support. Peer reviewers express concern about normalization methods and request alamethicin controls for proper internal calibration, indicating uncertainty about quantitative interpretation.

Partial overlap (C113, C121). LLM supports the proposed model that Bax/Bak function as outer membrane MPTP component in non-oligomerized state. Peer reviewers find this interpretation requires additional experimental confirmation beyond the presented data.

Minimal overlap (C103). LLM supports ABT-737/gossypol data showing regulation of Bax/Bak in necrosis. Peer reviewers question whether observed effects are MPTP-specific or general outer membrane properties.
Oxygen consumption data (C36-C44) evaluated only by LLM. No corresponding peer review assessment found for these specific claims about mitochondrial respiration maintenance in DKO MEFs.
Calcein-CoCl2 assay data (C78-C82) showing inner membrane opening occurs normally in DKO cells evaluated only by LLM. No direct peer review assessment of these specific claims.
Calcium imaging and ER calcium handling data (C92-C96) evaluated only by LLM. No corresponding peer review assessment found for these control experiments ruling out indirect effects.
Therapeutic implications (C127-C128) evaluated only by LLM as speculative. No corresponding peer review assessment of these broader translational claims.
Necroptosis resistance claims (C129-C130) evaluated only by LLM as uncertain due to lack of primary data. No corresponding peer review assessment found.
